idiom_name: test class implements the collaborator interface and passes this (delegate/lambda for one-method seams)
implementation_notes: xUnit/NUnit/MSTest test classes are ordinary classes, so the test case can implement the collaborator interface directly and pass this into the SUT's constructor or subscription method, recording into instance fields; xUnit instantiates the class once per test method, so that state is per-test by construction. When the contract is a single method and the SUT accepts a delegate (Action/Func) or an interface with one member, a lambda assigned in the test method replaces the whole-class shunt and keeps the recording local. Moq or NSubstitute take over once the double needs programmed expectations, argument matching or call-order verification -- the hand-written conformance stays the best fit while the collaborator's behaviour is just recording or a canned answer.
pitfalls: Conformance is all-or-nothing: IObserver<T> forces OnError and OnCompleted bodies even when the test only observes OnNext, so wide interfaces should not be shunted.
Instances are per-test in xUnit but can be reused across methods elsewhere (NUnit/MSTest with [SetUp]); recording fields that are not reset leak state between tests.

An interface member that matches a framework hook or another member's signature (explicit implementation needed) silently routes calls to the wrong body; use explicit interface implementation when names collide.
